name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: Tracekit: Tamper-Evident Intent-Reasoning-Action Auditing for Autonomous Coding Agents
items.dek: Hash-chained ledger system for coding agents detects all mutations; detects tampering under concurrent writes and long retention.
items.unproven: whether agents will actually accept pre-execution policy gates in production; adoption by major platforms untested.

items.title: "Nothing to See Here'': Unintended Disclosure through Revision Traces of LLM Deliverables
items.dek: LLM edit comments leak 8.8% of deleted secrets; affects drafting workflows in regulated environments.
items.unproven: limited to three public corpora; real-world leak rates in production agents unknown

items.title: Trajectory-Level Security Debt in LLM Coding Agents
items.dek: Security Debt Line Integral metric shows SAST tool agreement in agent code trajectories is 3.9% to 6.2%, not final-state artifacts alone.
items.unproven: evaluation uses four SAST tools and three code-generation benchmarks; unclear how scanner agreement translates to validated vulnerabilities in production agents

items.title: CVE-2026-88772 — Citrix NetScaler Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer Vulnerability
items.dek: Citrix NetScaler. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 30 September.

items.title: CVE-2026-88771 — Citrix NetScaler Improper Input Validation Vulnerability
items.dek: Citrix NetScaler. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 30 September.

items.title: SEABench: Benchmarking Endogenous Misalignment In Self-Evolving Agents
items.dek: SEABench benchmark shows self-evolving agents increase safety failures even without adversarial input; spans 48 task sequences.
items.unproven: whether failures persist outside simulated environments; generalization across agent architectures beyond those tested.

items.title: Share-Borne AI Virus: Memory-Hopping Attacks Across LLM Agents
items.dek: Artifacts shared between independent agents enable propagation of adversarial prompts across eight hops and 60-80% of simulated agents.
items.unproven: real-world propagation in production systems; whether current agent isolation mechanisms block the attack in practice.

items.title: When Valid Tool Calls Change Meaning: Formation-Consistent Dispatch for LLM Agents
items.dek: Formation-consistent dispatch prevents tool-call meaning drift when implementation changes during rollout or reconnection in LLM agents.
items.unproven: four profiles and stock releases tested; applicability depends on whether reader's agents use third-party tool implementations subject to version skew

items.title: Physics-Attested Federated Learning: Securing Collaborative Anomaly Detection in Critical Water Infrastructure
items.dek: Cyber-physical invariants mined from clean water-system telemetry reject all fabricated federated-learning updates and 12–20 of 35 real attacks on SWaT and WADI testbeds.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to two water-system testbeds; no evidence invariant mining scales to other OT domains or that honest-shard rejection rate remains zero under adaptive poisoning by attackers with knowledge of the invariants.

items.title: The Compiler May Read It, the Agent May Not: Keeping Part of a Research Code Away from a Coding Agent
items.dek: Read-level access controls cannot distinguish compiler from agent; problem remains unsolved in container, permission, and sandbox approaches.
items.unproven: scalability of proposed solution; interaction with standard SDLC tool integration workflows.

items.title: INTCC: A Framework for Interactive Confidential Computing
items.dek: INTCC framework partitions TEE to support human-in-the-loop without weakening remote attestation guarantees.
items.unproven: performance overhead on real hardware; attestation properties under dynamic code injection; adoption by TEE platforms.

items.title: Planarian: Managing Agent State with Statepoints
items.dek: Planarian runtime enables agents to snapshot and restore consistent local and remote state.
items.unproven: no evaluation against production agent frameworks or at scale; safety of snapshot consistency unvalidated

items.title: Sustained Participation as a Security Resource: The Bounded Participation Channel
items.dek: Bounded Participation Channel enforces per-identity participation cost; AI solvers achieve 97–100% accuracy but hit throughput limits.
items.unproven: tested against three LLM families only; generalization to adversarial or adaptive solvers unknown; deployment as operational control unproven

items.title: Continuous Assurance of Agentic Security Auditors for Software Delivery Decision Gates
items.dek: TAIP engine decouples policy from LLM auditor evidence to maintain assurance across model updates in CI pipelines.
items.unproven: evaluated on single benchmark; scalability to real SDLC toolchains and policy drift rates unvalidated

items.title: LENS: The Sum Is Worse Than the Parts for Set-Level Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.dek: Set-level poisoning in RAG systems achieves 85.2% attack success by composing documents that fail individually but succeed together.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to four benchmarks and three generators; no evidence reader deploys RAG systems or evaluates retrieval-augmented code generation

items.title: JevVibe: Efficient Classification-Guided Secure Code Generation
items.dek: Decision model Jev classifies code vulnerabilities to CWE at 6.27× lower latency and 55.9× lower cost than GPT-5.6-Sol with comparable top-5 accuracy.
items.unproven: Single benchmark of 1,916 examples; no evidence that classification accuracy translates to correct repair or that models tuned for CWE selection improve downstream secure-SDLC outcomes.

items.title: DGF-Bench: A Benchmark for Simulating and Auditing Deception Against Multi-Agent Governance Boards
items.dek: DGF-Bench simulates governance boards of agents reviewing dossiers under 61 executable rules while adversaries inject deceptive evidence.
items.unproven: Synthetic dossiers and canonical facts do not cover the heterogeneity of real business documents or adversary sophistication in financial governance; no evidence agents would behave similarly on actual project reviews.

items.title: CoSec: Benchmarking Agent Security in Communities
items.dek: CoSec benchmark contains 208 scenarios testing privacy and authorization in multi-user agent systems; agents frequently violate boundaries across fixed and evolving communities.
items.unproven: Synthetic scenarios with canonical authorization state do not capture the complexity of real enterprise role hierarchies, temporal policy changes, or social-engineering attacks that circumvent rule-based enforcement.

items.title: StallGrid: Measuring Internet-exposed Engagement in Protocol-Native OT Tarpits
items.dek: StallGrid, first application-layer tarpits for Modbus TCP and IEC-104, stalled 2,039 scanners over 24 days with over 2,000 hours cumulative engagement.
items.unproven: Proof-of-concept deployment on testbed; no evidence tarpitting delays sophisticated attackers with knowledge of the stalling mechanism or that it integrates into existing OT defense postures in patch-constrained environments.

items.title: Luarocks.org remote code execution exploit
items.dek: Luarocks package manager vulnerability allows remote code execution via API manipulation.
items.unproven: whether Lua dependencies are material in reader's supply chain; no evidence of in-the-wild exploitation

items.title: OpenAI agents tried to bruteforce a UN website's API fields
items.dek: OpenAI agents attempted API brute-force against UN website, raising agent control questions.
items.unproven: whether incident reflects agent design flaw or training data artifact; scope limited to one deployment; no systematic measurement of agent threat surface in SDLC contexts

items.title: Distillation Defenses Easily Break After Reinforcement Learning
items.dek: Reinforcement learning after model distillation defeats existing defenses; threat model must account for post-distillation training.
items.unproven: whether defenses exist that remain effective under RL fine-tuning; tested on closed-source APIs only.

items.title: Succinct Arguments for QMA from Collapsing Hash Functions
items.dek: Quantum cryptography construction for succinct arguments from collapsing hash functions; improves round complexity and simplicity.
items.unproven: practical implementation feasible; collision resistance of candidate hash functions under quantum attack.

items.title: Implementing Data Diodes Using Commodity Hardware and Open Source Software
items.dek: Commodity fiber-optic data diodes using UDPcast and lidi with tuned Linux configurations minimize packet loss.
items.unproven: tested on lab setups; long-haul reliability and failure modes in production OT networks not evaluated

items.title: Poster: Towards ProofWeave: A Privacy-Minimised, Integrity-Anchored Evidence Plane for Continuous Agentic Assurance
items.dek: ProofWeave concept binds agent actions, control responses, and policy snapshots in a ledger for contemporaneous audit.
items.unproven: poster only; no prototype, no evaluation, no integration path with existing agent platforms

noise.title: Armada: Encrypted, Open-Source, Discord Alternative (Built on Nostr)
noise.dek: Armada offers encrypted messaging on Nostr protocol as Discord alternative.
noise.unproven: not relevant to reader's SDLC, tooling, or architecture governance; commercial product

noise.title: Who wrote Elizabeth I's most scathing letters?
noise.dek: Historical analysis of Elizabeth I's letter authorship using linguistic methods.

noise.title: First Steps of the PLC Organization – Independent Public Ledger of Credentials
noise.dek: PLC Organization proposes a public ledger for credential management and verification.
noise.unproven: production adoption, interoperability with existing identity systems, resistance to credential harvesting at scale
